concerns.text: Tasks T025 (AntiSD Loop) and T028 (Timeout/Logging) are listed in Phase 3 but explicitly depend on T048 (Teacher Distribution Averaging) from Phase 2. The current ordering places T025/T028 before T048 is guaranteed to complete in the execution flow description, violating the 'Producer before Consumer' rule. T048 must precede T025.

Task T025 (AntiSD Loop) depends on T028-ENFORCE (Hard Timeout Enforcer). However, T028-ENFORCE is listed as a separate task in Phase 3, and the dependency note says 'Must be integrated... BEFORE training starts'. The task list does not explicitly enforce T028-ENFORCE execution prior to T025 in the dependency section, creating a risk of the training loop starting without the timeout guard.

Task T047 (Human Score Ingest) depends on T035-SIM (Human Evaluation Proxy Simulation). While the dependency is noted, T035-SIM itself depends on T035.1 (Reference Subset). The ordering block lists T047 as depending on T035.1 and T035-SIM, but the linear phase flow (Phase 4) groups them without explicit sequential enforcement between T035.1 -> T035-SIM -> T047, risking T047 running before T035-SIM generates the CSV.

Task T006 (Power Analysis) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but the description explicitly states 'Depends on T001.2'. A task with a hard dependency cannot be parallel-safe with its dependency. The [P] tag is semantically incorrect here and should be removed or the task re-ordered to strictly follow T001.2.

Task T017 (Context Simulator Sampling) and T017.1 (Context Simulator Exclusion & Reporting) are split but T017.1 depends on the output of T017 (exclusion log). The current listing places them sequentially, but the [P] tag is missing on T017.1 (correct), yet the dependency is not explicitly flagged in the 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section, relying on implicit phase ordering.
